newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Powerco bids for neighbouring Egmont - paper.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Powerco bids for neighbouring Egmont - paper.

text.p: Unlisted New Zealand regional power company Powerco Ltd has made a takeover bid for neighbouring electricity company Egmont Power worth NZ$124 million, The Dominion newspaper reported on Friday.

"The takeover may be a step toward the formation of a much bigger regional power company, with the potential for the enlarged Powerco-Egmont to team up with neighbouring Central Power," the newspaper said.
It quoted Powerco chairman Barry Upson apparently supporting this, saying "I think we would need to grow a bit bigger".
The companies were not available for comment on Friday.
The report said Egmont's owners, South Taranaki District Council, stood to get $90 million after the company's debt was paid off from the $124 million bid price.
Mayor Mary Burke told the Dominion the council had accepted the offer "in principle" subject to public consultation, and called the offer "very attractive".

Powerco has 70,000 customers and Egmont 12,000, and the larger company foresees operating savings of up to $4 million per year after full integration. Upson told the newspaper that part of the offer included a freeze on line charges from Egmont for the next two years, so revenue would not exceed forecasts.
Upson said that a debt-funded acquisition would be earnings enhancing for Powerco in time, as the earnings and operating savings would together exceed the funding costs of a deal.
